facts.text: Ottawa opened applications Oct. 15 for $430 million over five years for skilled trades training, mostly via an expanded Union Training and Innovation Program
Secretary of State for Labour John Zerucelli announced the funding
Facility/infrastructure expressions of interest close Nov. 12; shovel-ready projects sought for next spring
Equipment stream applications are ongoing, with the federal share temporarily raised to 70 per cent from 50
Innovation stream proposals are due Dec. 17
Nearly half the $430 million was already counted in a previous Liberal pledge ($8 billion, up to 100,000 trades workers)
Carney announced Team Canada Strong April 29, 2026: $6 billion over five years for 80,000-100,000 new Red Seal workers
Team Canada Strong's training component is $331 million over five years plus $18 million ongoing, including UTIP expansion
Spring Economic Update 2026 sets a target of 80,000-100,000 new Red Seal workers by 2030-31
ESDC's Oct. 15 release on the $430 million was published but its text could not be retrieved
The $8 billion (CP) and $6 billion (PMO) pledge figures are not reconciled
No Ontario-specific allocation of the $430 million has been confirmed
The program is national and application-based, open to unions and training providers, with no per-province formula
The equipment stream has no published closing date
Ontario and Canada investing $203,000+ for 75 Hamilton-area steel/manufacturing workers, part of a $228.8M program for up to 27,000 workers
Zerucelli says Canada needs more workers to build homes, infrastructure and major projects

missed.text: Zerucelli: Canada needs more workers to build homes, infrastructure and major projects, 'that's why we're investing in apprenticeship training facilities, modern equipment, and new approaches to training'
No breakdown of the $430 million by stream and no list of approved applicants has been published
